claim: Tailoring interventions to patient subgroups can improve intervention outcomes for various conditions.
source: Tailoring interventions to patient subgroups can improve intervention outcomes for various conditions.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract supported by established knowledge in precision medicine.

claim: Targeted therapies can lead to better health outcomes, such as increased life expectancy and remission rates, notably in cancer (Cutler, 2020).
source: Targeted therapies can lead to better health outcomes, such as increased life expectancy and remission rates, notably in cancer (Cutler, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cutler, 2020.

claim: Researchers are attempting to extend precision medicine approaches to conditions such as chronic pain (Reimer et al., 2021).
source: Researchers are now attempting to extend precision medicine approaches to other conditions such as chronic pain (Reimer et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Reimer et al., 2021.

claim: Advancements in artificial intelligence may soon broaden the use of personalisation for drug dosing (Rybak et al., 2020) and treatment selection (Ahmed et al., 2020).
source: Further, advancements in artificial intelligence may soon broaden the use of personalisation for drug dosing (Rybak et al., 2020) and treatment selection (Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rybak et al., 2020 and Ahmed et al., 2020.

claim: The influence of contextual factors in precision medicine remains relatively unexplored, despite experts highlighting their potential influence on intervention outcomes (Haga et al., 2009).
source: The influence of contextual factors in precision medicine remains relatively unexplored, despite experts highlighting their potential influence on intervention outcomes (Haga et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Haga et al., 2009.

claim: Contextual factors surrounding the intervention, such as verbal suggestions, patient expectations, social cues, and observational learning increase its effectiveness and reduce the associated side effects (Bernstein et al., 2020; Colloca and Barsky, 2020; Olson et al., 2021a).
source: Research in placebo science has shown that the contextual factors surrounding the intervention, such as verbal suggestions, patient expectations, social cues, and observational learning increase its effectiveness and reduce the associated side effects (Bernstein et al., 2020; Colloca and Barsky, 2020; Olson et al., 2021a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bernstein et al., 2020; Colloca and Barsky, 2020; Olson et al., 2021a.

claim: Some contextual factors can both modulate the effectiveness of inactive treatments in lab settings as well as increase the placebo effect of the real treatments in clinical settings (Blasini et al., 2018).
source: Some of these contextual factors can both modulate the effectiveness of inactive treatments in lab settings as well as increase the placebo effect of the real treatments in clinical settings (Blasini et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Blasini et al., 2018.

claim: Placebo effects are present for both subjective symptoms (e.g. pain, depression) and physiological ones (e.g. immune response, motor function) (Benedetti et al., 2005).
source: Additionally, these effects are present for both subjective symptoms (e.g. pain, depression) and physiological ones (e.g. immune response, motor function) (Benedetti et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Benedetti et al., 2005.

claim: The public generally believes that personalised interventions are fully unique.
source: The public generally believes that personalised interventions are fully unique, so much so that the field rebranded from 'personalised' to 'precision' medicine in an effort to dispel this exaggerated view (Juengst et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Juengst et al., 2016 regarding the rebranding.

claim: The field rebranded from 'personalised' to 'precision' medicine in an effort to dispel the exaggerated view that interventions are fully unique (Juengst et al., 2016).
source: The public generally believes that personalised interventions are fully unique, so much so that the field rebranded from 'personalised' to 'precision' medicine in an effort to dispel this exaggerated view (Juengst et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Juengst et al., 2016.

claim: Tailored interventions use information about individual genetics and biology—elements most people believe to define their individual essence (Gelman, 2003).
source: Despite the field's more modest focus on targeting patient subgroups, tailored interventions use information about individual genetics and biology—elements most people believe to define their individual essence (Gelman, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gelman, 2003.

claim: Learning about one's increased genetic risk for obesity may lead to lower self-efficacy, reduced perceived control over related behaviours (Beauchamp et al., 2011; Dar-Nimrod et al., 2014), and worse cardiorespiratory capacity (Turnwald et al., 2019).
source: For example, simply learning about one's increased genetic risk for obesity may lead to lower self-efficacy, reduced perceived control over related behaviours (Beauchamp et al., 2011; Dar-Nimrod et al., 2014), and worse cardiorespiratory capacity (Turnwald et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citations to Beauchamp et al., 2011; Dar-Nimrod et al., 2014; Turnwald et al., 2019.

claim: Learning one has a protective genetic makeup may cause opposite results to learning about increased genetic risk (Turnwald et al., 2019), regardless of the actual genes involved.
source: learning one has a protective genetic makeup may cause the opposite results (Turnwald et al., 2019), regardless of the actual genes involved.
evidence: Supported by citation to Turnwald et al., 2019.

claim: Treatments that are more elaborate, invasive (de Craen et al., 2000; Hróbjartsson and Gøtzsche, 2010; Meissner et al., 2013), or use complex technology may cause larger improvements (Kaptchuk et al., 2000; Kaptchuk et al., 2008).
source: Indeed, studies in placebo science show that treatments that are more elaborate, invasive (de Craen et al., 2000; Hróbjartsson and Gøtzsche, 2010; Meissner et al., 2013), or use complex technology may cause larger improvements (Kaptchuk et al., 2000; Kaptchuk et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to de Craen et al., 2000; Hróbjartsson and Gøtzsche, 2010; Meissner et al., 2013; Kaptchuk et al., 2000; Kaptchuk et al., 2008.

claim: Tailoring treatments requires more physician attention and the involvement of practitioners specifically trained in therapeutic communication, such as genetic counsellors (Austin et al., 2014; Kohut et al., 2019).
source: Given the complexity of the procedure, tailoring treatments requires more physician attention and the involvement of practitioners specifically trained in therapeutic communication, such as genetic counsellors (Austin et al., 2014; Kohut et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Austin et al., 2014; Kohut et al., 2019.

claim: Providing enhanced information about a treatment can increase the effects of already potent drugs like opioids (Amanzio et al., 2001; Benedetti et al., 2003).
source: Similarly, placebo studies show that providing enhanced information about a treatment can increase the effects of already potent drugs like opioids (Amanzio et al., 2001; Benedetti et al., 2003)

claim: Positive communication strategies may reduce the side effects of sham pills (Barnes et al., 2019; Colloca and Finniss, 2012).

evidence: Supported by citations to Barnes et al., 2019; Colloca and Finniss, 2012.

source: More broadly, a warm and empathetic encounter can improve outcomes for active and inactive treatments in clinical settings (Blasini et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Blasini et al., 2018.

source: The conditioning phase of the task was used to demonstrate the machine's effectiveness. Participants received 4 pain stimulations at 80/100 level pain when the machine was turned off and 4 stimulations at 20/100 level pain when the machine was turned on, in a counterbalanced order.

source: Participants receiving a placebo they thought was personalised reported nearly twice the reduction in pain intensity (38%; standardised β=−0.50 [−1.08, 0.08], p=.044) and unpleasantness (41%; β=−0.52 [–1.04, –0.001], p=.025, Figures 4 and 5) as those in the control group (19% and 27%, respectively).

claim: Participants receiving a placebo they thought was personalised reported nearly twice the reduction in pain unpleasantness (41%; β=−0.52 [–1.04, –0.001], p=.025) as those in the control group (27%) in the feasibility study.
source: Participants receiving a placebo they thought was personalised reported nearly twice the reduction in pain intensity (38%; standardised β=−0.50 [−1.08, 0.08], p=.044) and unpleasantness (41%; β=−0.52 [–1.04, –0.001], p=.025, Figures 4 and 5) as those in the control group (19% and 27%, respectively).

claim: Testing placebo effects with experimental pain may have led to a conservative estimate of the placebo effect and may not map directly onto the clinical experience of chronic pain.
source: Nevertheless, testing placebo effects with experimental pain may have led to a conservative estimate of the placebo effect and may not map directly onto the clinical experience of chronic pain.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a limitation based on inference.

claim: Patients differ from healthy participants on many characteristics, including their motivation to get better (National Cancer Institute, 2021), the mechanisms through which they experience placebo effects (short- or long-term; Vase et al., 2005), and the methods of assessing pain ratings (immediate versus retrospective).
source: Patients differ from healthy participants on many characteristics, including their motivation to get better (National Cancer Institute, 2021), the mechanisms through which they experience placebo effects (short- or long-term; Vase et al., 2005), and the methods of assessing pain ratings (immediate versus retrospective).
evidence: Supported by citations to National Cancer Institute, 2021 and Vase et al., 2005.

claim: The sample size, exclusion criteria, and analyses were pre-registered online (https://osf.io/dcs98).
source: The sample size, exclusion criteria, and analyses were pre-registered online (https://osf.io/dcs98).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the pre-registration.

claim: The procedure was based on studies of complex placebo interventions (Olson et al., 2021a; Olson and Raz, 2021c).
source: The procedure was based on studies of complex placebo interventions (Olson et al., 2021a; Olson and Raz, 2021c)
evidence: Supported by citations to Olson et al., 2021a and Olson and Raz, 2021c.

claim: Recent studies suggest that traits such as interoceptive awareness (attention to one's physical sensations) and openness to experience predict the magnitude of placebo response (Vachon-Presseau et al., 2018).
source: Recent studies suggest that traits such as interoceptive awareness (attention to one's physical sensations) and openness to experience predict the magnitude of placebo response (Vachon-Presseau et al., 2018)
evidence: Supported by citation to Vachon-Presseau et al., 2018.

claim: Traits such as need for uniqueness (the desire to be seen as different from others) may moderate the specific placebo effects of personalisation.
source: we additionally expected that other traits such as need for uniqueness (the desire to be seen as different from others) may moderate the specific placebo effects of personalisation.
evidence: This is a stated hypothesis that was later confirmed by data.

claim: The placebo machine's design (over a dozen of switches and dials) allowed the researchers to simulate complex personalisation to the participants' profile.
source: The machine's design (over a dozen of switches and dials) allowed us to simulate complex personalisation to the participants' profile.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study materials with reference to Figure 2.

claim: The conditioning phase was used to demonstrate the machine's effectiveness by covertly reducing the intensity of pain stimulations when the machine was turned on.
source: In the conditioning phase, we simulated machine effectiveness by covertly reducing the intensity of pain stimulations when the machine was turned on.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study methodology with reference to Figure 3.

claim: For the testing phase, the temperature was kept stable and the placebo effect was quantified as the difference between the trials with the machine off and on.
source: For the testing phase, we kept the temperature stable and quantified the placebo effect as the difference between the trials with the machine off and on.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study methodology with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The gap between off–on temperatures was reduced to increase the believability of the machine's effect in the confirmatory study.
source: We reduced the gap between off–on temperatures to increase the believability of the machine's effect in the confirmatory study.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study methodology.

claim: Several participants in both groups reported increases in pain ratings from using the machine.
source: Several participants in both groups also reported increases in pain ratings from using the machine.
evidence: This is a direct report of data from the confirmatory study.

claim: The main limitations of the study are its focus on healthy participants, the use of an inactive treatment, a sample with imbalanced genders, and the focus on subjective outcomes.
source: The main limitations of the study are its focus on healthy participants, the use of an inactive treatment, a sample with imbalanced genders, and the focus on subjective outcomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of limitations.

claim: These factors restricted the generalisation of the findings to clinical settings.
source: Together, these factors restricted the generalisation of our findings to clinical settings.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a limitation based on inference.

claim: If confirmed in clinical settings, the findings may have implications beyond the field of precision medicine and healthcare.
source: If confirmed in clinical settings, our findings may have implications beyond the field of precision medicine and healthcare.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future implications.

claim: Individual tailoring is increasingly becoming the focus of consumer products and experiences; a large marketing organisation recently declared 'personalisation' as the word of the year (ANA, 2019).
source: Individual tailoring is increasingly becoming the focus of consumer products and experiences; a large marketing organisation recently declared 'personalisation' as the word of the year (ANA, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to ANA, 2019.

claim: Various companies now sell personalised diets based on nutrigenomics or personalised exercise plans based on sportomics; others promise personalised learning approaches based on behavioural genetics.
source: Various companies now sell personalised diets based on nutrigenomics or personalised exercise plans based on sportomics; others promise personalised learning approaches based on behavioural genetics, to name a few.
evidence: This is a statement based on general knowledge of the market.

claim: Several of these fields are in their early stages (Guest et al., 2019; Sellami et al., 2021) and it remains unclear what the effectiveness of some such tailored approaches may be (Janssens et al., 2008).
source: However, several of these fields are in their early stages (Guest et al., 2019; Sellami et al., 2021) and it remains unclear what the effectiveness of some such tailored approaches may be (Janssens et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Guest et al., 2019; Sellami et al., 2021; Janssens et al., 2008.

claim: The results raise the possibility that placebo effects involved in personalisation may play a relevant role in the context of the growing interest in precision medicine.
source: Our results raise the possibility that placebo effects involved in personalisation may play a relevant role in the context of the growing interest in precision medicine.
evidence: This is an inference based on the study results.

claim: The personalisation process was strong enough to influence the perception of thermal pain stimulations.
source: In this study, we show that the personalisation process was strong enough to influence the perception of thermal pain stimulations.
evidence: This is a direct interpretation of the study results.

claim: These effects could be potentially even more pronounced in clinical trials and medical contexts, for conditions with both objective and subjective symptoms that are amenable to placebo effects (Wampold et al., 2005), or for complex interventions such as diet change.
source: These effects could be potentially even more pronounced in clinical trials and medical contexts, for conditions with both objective and subjective symptoms that are amenable to placebo effects (Wampold et al., 2005), or for complex interventions such as diet change.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future implications with citation to Wampold et al., 2005.

claim: Some interventions known to be susceptible to placebos (e.g. immunotherapy) may be more amenable to context optimisation than others (e.g., Alzheimer's therapy; Benedetti et al., 2005).
source: Some interventions known to be susceptible to placebos (e.g. immunotherapy) may be more amenable to context optimisation than others (e.g., Alzheimer's therapy; Benedetti et al., 2005)
evidence: Supported by citation to Benedetti et al., 2005.

claim: Patients from more individualistic cultures and possessing specific personality traits may benefit from enhanced tailoring while others may be hindered by it.
source: patients from more individualistic cultures and possessing specific personality traits may benefit from enhanced tailoring while others may be hindered by it.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future implications.

claim: Initiatives like the United States' 'All of Us Program' and the UK's Biobank are collecting millions of data points on biomarkers of disease in a move towards routinely personalised healthcare.
source: Initiatives like the United States' 'All of Us Program' and the UK's Biobank are collecting millions of data points on biomarkers of disease in a move towards routinely personalised healthcare.
evidence: This is a statement based on general knowledge of these initiatives.

claim: Contextual factors may be a hidden element to understand and harness in this new era of medicine.
source: We show that contextual factors may be a hidden element to understand and harness in this new era of medicine.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study results.

claim: Clinicians may be able to optimise the placebo effect of personalisation by improving therapeutic communication.
source: If the studies in clinical contexts with real treatments find a similar or larger placebo effect due to personalisation, clinicians may be able to optimise it when delivering treatments. Precision drug dosing is set to become more available to the general public by potentially targeting a broader range of diseases (Rybak et al., 2020); physicians may be able to enhance this placebo effect by improving therapeutic communication.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about clinical implications with citation to Rybak et al., 2020.

claim: Physicians could describe in detail how patients' biological variability would be used to personalise the treatment or drug dose, or they could highlight the general complexity of the personalisation procedure.
source: For example, they could describe in detail how patients' biological variability would be used to personalise the treatment or drug dose, or they could highlight the general complexity of the personalisation procedure.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about clinical implications.

claim: Physicians could simply emphasise the likely increase in intervention effectiveness due to its personalisation.
source: Physicians could also simply emphasise the likely increase in intervention effectiveness due to its personalisation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about clinical implications.

claim: A lot of medicine is already personalised to various metrics even before factoring in genetic testing.
source: Outside of personalised treatments, physicians could still harness the allure of tailoring. A lot of medicine is already personalised to various metrics even before factoring in genetic testing
evidence: This is a statement based on general knowledge of medical practice.

claim: Focusing patients' attention on how treatment is personalised to their tests or biological particularities may potentially enhance the effectiveness of more typical treatments.
source: focusing patients' attention on that fact and how it is personalised to their tests or biological particularities may potentially enhance the effectiveness of more typical treatments.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about clinical implications.

claim: Placebo studies demonstrate that verbally emphasising the helpfulness of drugs like morphine further increases their effect (Benedetti et al., 2003).
source: Indeed, placebo studies demonstrate that verbally emphasising the helpfulness of drugs like morphine further increases their effect (Benedetti et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Benedetti et al., 2003.

claim: One could take a similar approach to emphasise the existing personalisation for various treatments.
source: One could take a similar approach to emphasise the existing personalisation for various treatments.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about clinical implications.
